messages:
jess: FYI customer on dedicated pool (acct: acme-io) started getting intermittent 429s and a sudden billing jump around 00:15 UTC. They say reserved pool shows ~60% free in Console. Can someone triage?

mike: Noted. Do we have request ids or an example timestamp from the customer? 429s + billing spike usually means fallback to hosted or double-counting during retries.

jess: Customer supplied one request id: req_8a7f2f22. Sample curl they ran: `curl -i -H \"Authorization: Bearer <key>\" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'` They saw `HTTP/1.1 429` with `x-rate-limit-retry-after: 0.2` then a few seconds later multiple successful calls billed at hosted rate.

anita: Pinging eng-runtime + oncall. Oncall cheng, can you pull the reserved-pool logs for that window and the token-bucket state for pool acme-io?

cheng: Got it, pulling logs now. Quick note: our rate-limiter emits debug lines like `rl:pool=acme-io tokens=8/20 window_ms=1000 route=/v1/generate`. Searching around 00:10-00:20 UTC.

deploy-bot: deploy:release/rl-adjust-2025 rolled at 2025-02-14T23:58:12Z to cluster-eu-prod.

mike: That deploy might be relevant. Any post-deploy telemetry changes?

cheng: Found a pattern. During a short spike we have many small concurrent requests fan out across 8 serving pods; the reserved-pool bucket is per-instance+global hybrid. Some instances hit local bucket 0 -> 429, then requests retry and are routed to other pods which have free tokens. Those succeed but the fallback routing path uses the hosted cluster as a last-resort in a small window when inter-pod routing latency exceeds 150ms. The customer saw 429 then success on hosted.

jess: So reserved pool not truly exhausted, it's distribution skew + routing latency causing hosted fallback. That explains billing jump. Any quick mitigation?

anita: Two options: 1) temporarily increase pool burst window (gives bigger local bucket) or 2) disable hosted fallback for that customer's pool (pin to dedicated) until we patch. Both require infra action.

mike: Before we change config, can we reproduce in staging? I can run a small load test that simulates fanout: 200 clients with short TTL and jitter. Will post script.

mike: repro script (python):
```
import requests, threading
for i in range(200):
  threading.Thread(target=lambda: requests.post('https://staging.redwood/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer test'}, json={'prompt':'x'*10})).start()
```

cheng: Tried a constrained run in staging. Observed identical token-starvation with our rl config. Also saw `rl-debug` lines with a race: local bucket depletion updated after decision to fallback. Looks like race between token check and book-keeping when requests hit multiple pods via LB.

mike: That suggests an off-by-one timing window in `claim_tokens()` under high concurrency. Patch idea: change atomic check+decrement to a single raft-backed op for heavy pools OR widen `local_token_window_ms` from 250 -> 500 as a short-term config. Which do we want?

anita: Short-term: widen local window for acme-io to 1000ms and set `no_hosted_fallback=true` on their pool. Engineering: we'll schedule a proper fix in runtime (serializing claims) target next patch.

lucy: I spoke with the customer. They're ok with temporary config but want clarity on billing. They were billed at hosted rates for ~320 requests. Can billing team review and possibly credit the hosted fallback portion?

billing-bot: Billing ticket created: BILL-5421 linked to support thread 2290012345. Attach logs and cost delta export.

mike: For the support ticket, please include: 1) `rl` logs around req_8a7f2f22, 2) LB routing table snapshot, 3) hosted fallback events list, 4) customer consent to config change.

cheng: Collected logs and observed this snippet around the failing request:
```
[00:15:12.142] rl:pool=acme-io pod=pod-7 tokens_before=0 tokens_after=0 decision=429 req=req_8a7f2f22
[00:15:12.147] lb:route req=req_8a7f2f22 retry=1 routed_to=hosted-03
[00:15:12.153] hosted:accept req=req_8a7f2f22 status=200 cost_profile=hosted-standard
```

anita: I pushed a config change to prod for acme-io: `local_token_window_ms=1000`, `no_hosted_fallback=true` and a temporary `burst_tokens=40`. Monitor for 30m. I also disabled the new rl-adjust release (rolled back) to see if that helps.

mike: Thanks. Created support note for the customer with the config changes and mitigation. Also included recommended client-side change: exponential backoff with capped retries and prefer-serve header to avoid cross-pool fanout. Example header: `Prefer-Serve: dedicated`

lucy: Customer accepted temporary change and asked for ETA on permanent fix + code-level explanation.

cheng: Root-cause for follow-up: race in token accounting when pod-local bucket and global view disagree under LB jitter. Action items: ENG-11234 add atomic token claim path; ENG-11235 add e2e test for fanout.

mike: Billing asked to queue potential credit if hosted fallback shows cost > $X. billing-bot already created the ticket.

jess: Closing loop with customer now. Will update thread after 30m monitor. Thanks all :thumbsup:
